              - generic [ref=e100]:
                - link "Cedric Howell" [ref=e104] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/File:Raymond_Brownwell_and_Cedric_Howell_France_P00046.084_(Howell_cropped).JPG
                  - img "Cedric Howell" [ref=e105]
                - paragraph [ref=e106]:
                  - link "Cedric Howell" [ref=e108] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: /wiki/Cedric_Howell
                  - text: (17 June 1896 – 10 December 1919) was an Australian
                  - link "flying ace" [ref=e109] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: /wiki/Flying_ace
                  - text: of the First World War. He enlisted in the
                  - link "Australian Imperial Force" [ref=e110] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: /wiki/First_Australian_Imperial_Force
                  - text: in 1916 and was posted to the 46th Battalion on the
                  - link "Western Front" [ref=e111] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: /wiki/Western_Front_(World_War_I)
                  - text: . In November 1916, he was accepted for a transfer to the
                  - link "Royal Flying Corps" [ref=e112] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: /wiki/Royal_Flying_Corps
                  - text: and was shipped to the United Kingdom for flight training. Graduating as a pilot, he was commissioned as a
                  - link "second lieutenant" [ref=e113] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: /wiki/Second_lieutenant
                  - text: and posted to
                  - link "No. 45 Squadron RFC" [ref=e114] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: /wiki/No._45_Squadron_RAF
                  - text: in France during October 1917; two months later, the unit sailed to the
                  - link "Italian theatre" [ref=e115] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: /wiki/Italian_front_(World_War_I)
                  - text: . Howell spent eight months flying operations over Italy, conducting attacks against ground targets and engaging in sorties against aerial forces and he was credited with shooting down a total of nineteen aircraft. He was awarded the
                  - link "Distinguished Service Order" [ref=e116] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: /wiki/Distinguished_Service_Order
                  - text: ", the"
                  - link "Military Cross" [ref=e117] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: /wiki/Military_Cross
                  - text: and
                  - link "Distinguished Flying Cross" [ref=e118] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: /wiki/Distinguished_Flying_Cross_(United_Kingdom)
                  - text: . He was posted back to the United Kingdom in July 1918. In 1919, Howell was killed while taking part in the
                  - link "England-to-Australia air race" [ref=e119] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: /wiki/1919_England_to_Australia_flight
                  - text: .

                  - /url: /wiki/File:Wfm_orkney_map.png
                  - img "Map of Orkney" [ref=e367]
                - generic [ref=e368]: Map of Orkney
              - paragraph [ref=e369]:
                - link "There are more than 70 islands and skerries" [ref=e371] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/List_of_Orkney_islands
                - text: in
                - link "Orkney" [ref=e372] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Orkney
                - text: ", an archipelago located 16 kilometres (9.9 mi) north of mainland"
                - link "Scotland" [ref=e373] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Scotland
                - text: . Twenty islands are permanently inhabited. In addition to the
                - link "Mainland" [ref=e374] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Mainland,_Orkney
                - text: ", there are three groups of islands. The North and South Isles lie respectively north and south of Mainland, and the"
                - link "Pentland Skerries" [ref=e375] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Pentland_Skerries
                - text: are a group of small islands in the
                - link "Pentland Firth" [ref=e376] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Pentland_Firth
                - text: ", a dangerous stretch of water between mainland Scotland and the larger islands of Orkney, through which run the strongest tidal streams in Britain. The islands of"
                - link "South Ronaldsay" [ref=e377] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/South_Ronaldsay
                - text: ","
                - link "Burray" [ref=e378] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Burray
                - text: ","
                - link "Lamb Holm" [ref=e379] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Lamb_Holm
                - text: and
                - link "Glimps Holm" [ref=e380] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Glimps_Holm
                - text: are connected to the Orkney Mainland by a series of
                - link "causeways" [ref=e381] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Causeway
                - text: known as the
                - link "Churchill Barriers" [ref=e382] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Churchill_Barriers
                - text: . Most of the islands have bedrock formed from
                - link "Old Red Sandstone" [ref=e383] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Old_Red_Sandstone
                - text: ", which is about 400 million years old, and was laid down in the"
                - link "Devonian" [ref=e384] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Devonian
                - text: period. The archipelago has been continuously inhabited for thousands of years, and is home to the
                - link "World Heritage Site" [ref=e385] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/World_Heritage_Site
                - text: of the
                - link "Heart of Neolithic Orkney" [ref=e386] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Heart_of_Neolithic_Orkney
                - text: . The islands all fall within the
                - link "Orkney Islands Council" [ref=e387] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Orkney_Islands_Council
                - text: area and have a total population of 21,958 (as of 2022).
                - generic [ref=e388]:
                  - text: (
                  - link "This list" [ref=e390] [cursor=pointer]:

                - link "Islands of Scotland" [ref=e393] [cursor=pointer]:

              - paragraph [ref=e417]:
                - link "Graphium colonna" [ref=e420] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Graphium_colonna
                - text: ", the black swordtail or mamba swordtail, is a species in the family Papilionidae, the"
                - link "swallowtail butterflies" [ref=e421] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Swallowtail_butterfly
                - text: . It is found widely across sub-Saharan Africa, from West Africa to eastern and southern Africa. The butterfly is predominantly black with green markings and the characteristic "tail" on the hindwing. The species breeds throughout the warmer months, and its
                - link "caterpillars" [ref=e422] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Caterpillar
                - text: feed on plants in the genera
                - link "Artabotrys" [ref=e424] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Artabotrys
                - text: ","
                - link "Uvaria" [ref=e426] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Uvaria
                - text: and
                - link "Annona" [ref=e428] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Annona
                - text: . Graphium colonna belongs to the clade antheus of the genus
                - link "Graphium" [ref=e430] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Graphium_(butterfly)
                - text: and was first described by
                - link "Christopher Ward" [ref=e431] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Christopher_Ward_(entomologist)
                - text: in 1873. This G. colonna butterfly was photographed in
                - link "Maputo National Park" [ref=e432] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /wiki/Maputo_National_Park
                - text: ", Mozambique."
